recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. FHIR-9646 is already applied in current core source; future response-handling adjustments should be made under the later messaging issues rather than by reopening this DSTU2 restructuring issue.
issue_request: FHIR-9646 was Published/Persuasive for restructuring the FHIR-core messaging page: separate generic messaging guidance from REST-specific $process-message content, move synchronous/asynchronous exchange patterns into the generic discussion, keep only a short $process-message overview with details on the operation page, clarify asynchronous response handling, and add non-REST protocol discussion.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit 7d3bfc0e87e612ca3946b47ff9d2270625bfde1d, 'GF9646 - restructure messaging page' / SVN build revision 14495, which moved sync/async prose out of the $process-message section and shortened the local $process-message text to point to the operation definition.
additional_context: source/messaging.html is linked from source/documentation.html and MessageHeader is active in source/fhir.ini. Later applied/published messaging decisions FHIR-25252, FHIR-25465, FHIR-40518, FHIR-40519, FHIR-40501, and FHIR-27544 refined response-message and transfer-protocol wording and are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source has generic messaging assumptions and message exchange patterns before $process-message, a brief $process-message summary with details in the MessageHeader OperationDefinition, REST-specific content under the REST relationship section, and non-REST transfer examples in the generic assumptions section. Older wording that every async acknowledgement be a message Bundle should not be reintroduced because newer decisions allow zero-or-more response messages and HTTP-level acknowledgements.

related_jiras.note: Clarified that $process-message can be acknowledged with a bare HTTP response and does not always require a response Bundle; already represented on the combined branch.
Clarified that message requests typically, not always, have response messages and notification scenarios may use HTTP-level acknowledgement; already represented on the combined branch.
Changed the messaging introduction to zero-or-more response messages, superseding older one-or-more assumptions; already represented on the combined branch.
Refined the same messaging page's protocol-transfer wording for non-REST mechanisms; already represented on the combined branch.
Added Apache Kafka to the non-REST messaging transport examples now present in the generic assumptions section; already represented on the combined branch.
Aligned $process-message wording with zero-or-more response messages; already represented on the combined branch.
